title: list.pop()
summary: Remove and return an item — O(1) from the end, O(n) from anywhere else.
description: `pop()` with no argument makes a list a perfectly good stack. `pop(0)` makes it a bad queue, because every remaining element shifts left.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Position to remove; the last item by default.

raises.when: The list is empty, or the index is out of range.

examples.title: From the front — correct but O(n)
The O(1) queue
examples.code:
from collections import deque
q = deque([1, 2, 3])
print(q.popleft(), list(q))

real_world_usage: Undo stacks, depth-first traversal, and draining a work list.

common_mistakes.mistake: pop(0) in a loop to drain a queue
Popping while iterating the same list
common_mistakes.fix: Indices shift and elements are skipped. Iterate a copy or use a while loop with explicit bounds.
IndexError. Test the list first, or catch it.

performance_notes: O(1) at the end, O(n) elsewhere because of the shift. deque is O(1) at both ends.
